groups.note: County, municipal, school, and special-district names are keyed from official Sublette clerk general summaries (official 2022 DocumentCenter View/4109 via Wayback after the live slug was removed; official 2024 View/6118; official 2026 View/8211), official Town of Pinedale council and 2026 municipal results pages, and the official Town of Marbleton council page. Official 2014–2020 clerk general canvasses were not found on the live /110/Election-Information page or on the February 8, 2023 Wayback capture of that page, so January 2015–2022 county, municipal, school, and special-district rows are largely Not yet collected rather than invented. Multi-county legislative seats use official SOS district-wide Total rows, with the official Sublette share noted, for every keyed year (2012, 2016, 2020, and 2024 S14; 2012–2026 H20; 2012–2020 H22). Official SOS two-column pages were cut at the next district header. After 2022 redistricting, official SOS H22 Sublette rows are dashes (Lincoln and Teton only); official Sublette H22 is ended at January 2023 rather than inventing a holdover. Official Lincoln slivers for Sublette County School District #9 are combined into the official whole-district result in 2022, 2024, and 2026; ranking is unchanged, including the official 2026 2-year seat where the Lincoln portion alone had Taylor Moceika ahead of Brock Forrest McLain (combined McLain 547, Moceika 319). The official Town of Big Piney site returned a Cloudflare challenge from this collection environment, and no official council roster, minutes, canvass, or Wayback capture of an official town page was retrieved, so Big Piney mayor and council stay Not yet collected. Secondary directories are not used. Official 2022 soil-conservation headings are unlabeled (Urban/Rural/At-Large are not printed), so those two official 2022 winners stay on the generic title. The official 2026 proclamation placed a question to reduce the commission from five to three; official canvass AGAINST 2,659 (72.49%), so the board remains five members. Write-in-only official contests with no named certified winner are not seated.

groups.note: Supreme Court justices and the Chancery Court judge are the people in office this January, from official Wyoming Judicial Branch dates and official retention results (shared with other counties). Official 2026 Sublette clerk retentions for Justice Hill, Justice Jarosh, and Chancery Judge Burningham are those statewide retentions. Local rows are 9th Judicial District judges (Sublette, Teton, and Fremont). Full names and appointment dates are taken from official Wyoming Judicial Branch 9th JD court pages already used in the Teton history, and official Sublette named retentions are cited (2024 Melissa M. Owens, Katharine G. McKay — official clerk spelling KATHERINE G. MCKAY — Daniel M. Stebner, and John Labuda; 2026 Jason M. Conder, Weisman, and Coombs). Official 2022 Sublette clerk prints two unnamed 9th JD circuit retentions (YES 2,590 / NO 490 and YES 2,483 / NO 527); those official totals are not assigned to a named judge. Judges of other districts are not copied here.
